_README: Two-legged ties in play, and the context a 90-minute market cannot see.
Written 2026-08-13 after Hammarby. That leg was taken as a routine home
favourite; the tie was level from a 0-0 first leg, so the second leg was a
must-win, and 0-1 down with a red card on 54 minutes it went 85% -> 17%.
None of that was visible in the price, and the first-leg score had already
passed through the morning's own research without being written down.
preflight's TIE gate reads this file. A soccer leg on a match listed here
with no first_leg recorded is a FAIL, not a warning: the whole point is
Keys are the match as the board labels it. 'first_leg' is the score of leg
one written from the SIDE THE LEG IS ON. 'standing' is what that makes the
aggregate before kickoff. 'note' is the incentive read -- a tie already won
means rotation, a level tie means both sides push.

Rakow-Hammarby.note: LEVEL TIE = must-win second leg. Both goal expectations up, so an under is worse than its price and the DC is far more volatile than a home favourite's number suggests.

Bohemians-Midtjylland.note: Comfortable. Expect rotation; under improves, favourite's 90-minute DC gets shakier than the price implies.

CFR Cluj-Tromso.note: DEAD RUBBER. Nothing to play for on either side. Tromso only -165 at home after a 5-0 away win is the book pricing the reserve XI. Under is materially better than it looks; the DC carries lineup risk that is close to binary.

Valur-Nordsjaelland.note: Comfortable. Same rotation shape as Midtjylland, smaller.

Besiktas-Hradec Kralove.note: Bet as TO ADVANCE, which prices the aggregate by construction -- but the first leg is still unrecorded and a 90-minute market on this match must not be taken until it is.

Hearts-Benfica.note: Bet as TO ADVANCE. Hearts +10000 and Benfica locked means the book sees the tie as effectively over; record the first leg before touching a 90-minute market here.
